critical_operation.desc: Dangerous configuration: this sudoers rule grants app passwordless execution as any user for every command. It directly defeats the later USER app privilege boundary because a compromised process can recover full root without credentials.

entry_point.code:
RUN useradd -m -s /bin/bash app \
  && echo "app ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL" > /etc/sudoers.d/app
entry_point.desc: Explicit dangerous state: this RUN block creates app and immediately associates it with a passwordless full-sudo rule. Unlike the first three entries, the vulnerable privilege state is declared here rather than inherited from a missing USER boundary.

trace.code:

trace.desc: Declaration: app is created and given NOPASSWD:ALL, establishing a persistent capability to recover root.
Nominal transition: USER app changes the active uid but does not remove the full passwordless sudo capability declared above.
Privilege proof: after USER app, the build still uses sudo to chmod a system path, demonstrating that the app user can exercise root.
Runtime materialization: the nonroot-named entrypoint runs as app, but that app identity carries passwordless full-root escalation.
